mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer demand for new construction, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved economic growth expectations and corporate earnings outlook.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST increases by at least 0.5% over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 0.5% indicates active monetary tightening, which increases discount rates for equity valuation and typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 0.1% and UNRATE decreases > 0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls as specified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% during monetary tightening cycles compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates, typically resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.2 percentage points in one month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong manufacturing output and economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to improved corporate profitability outlook.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO increases by at least 0.5% over the prior quarter.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL above 280.0 indicates elevated inflation, which typically triggers expectations of aggressive monetary tightening and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 280.0.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 280.0 and FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5%, it signals an early phase of monetary tightening that increases equity volatility and typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances meeting the CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A very low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 3.5%) in late-cycle expansions signals labor market exhaustion and impending economic slowdown, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE falls below 3.5%.
